links.outcome: Physician sentiment on alert placement, design, workflow fit, and reasons for ignoring the alert
links.effect: Alert placement was largely intuitive and nonintrusive, and design was viewed positively. Some physicians ignored it because it was redundant, irrelevant, or lacked enough information. Overall effect on workflow was marginally positive.
links.quote: The alert placement was noted to be largely intuitive and nonintrusive.

screen.reason: Qualitative evaluation of physician perceptions pre- and post-implementation of an ED predictive CDS alert for opioid-related events and recidivism; it explores user interface and adoption but does not formally test a specific guardrail or deployment practice.
